From: marissa.cole@redwood.com

Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-05T08:32:00-07:00
Subject: MAP test matrix and TTFT definitions

Hi Sara / Laura —

Attaching the test matrix workbook (HS_MAP_TestMatrix.xlsx). Quick notes on how we’ll measure: 
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) measured from request ingress to first token emitted over the streaming API. We’ll report P50/P95/P99 across the run and breakdown by sequence-length buckets (short: <64 tokens, medium: 64–256, long: >256).
- Streaming tail lag: measured as time between first token and final token for streaming responses; useful for long completion scenarios.
- Throughput: requests/sec measured at the Redwood gateway. Concurrency: number of simultaneous open KV/stream sessions.
- Environment baseline: Redwood hosted (dedicated pool) — A100s, model: gpt-open-7b-q4, quantized runtime, batching disabled except for controlled concurrency trials.

Planned test sweeps:
1) Baseline TTFT sweep (single session, sequence-length buckets)
2) Concurrency ramp: 1 -> 50 -> 100 -> 180 -> 220 -> 300 (sustained for 5 min at each step, record P50/P95/P99)
3) Burst-stress: short 30s bursts to 500 concurrent connections to test graceful degradation and fallback.
4) Stability run: 2-hour sustained 200 concurrency run to check memory/KV cache impact.

Deliverables: per-sweep CSVs with raw samples, summary report (P50/P95/P99), and recommended configuration changes (batching/quantization/profile) for target SLOs.

If that looks good we’ll slot you for a dedicated window Mar 16–18.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Performance Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: monica.patel@redwood.com

Cc: sara.jenkins@healthsync.com
Date: 2027-03-09T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Initial perf run results (baseline & small concurrency sweep)

Team / Sara —

We executed the baseline and a small concurrency sweep on Mar 8 using the HealthSync prompt set. Summary highlights (all numbers in milliseconds for TTFT unless noted):

Baseline (single session): model=gpt-open-7b-q4, runtime=quantized
- Short (<64): P50=72ms, P95=142ms, P99=245ms
- Medium (64–256): P50=125ms, P95=268ms, P99=410ms
- Long (>256): P50=210ms, P95=520ms, P99=980ms

Small concurrency sweep (sustained 5 min at each step, warm caches):
- 1 -> 50 concurrent:
  - 50 conc: TTFT P50=95ms, P95=320ms, P99=675ms; throughput observed ~22 reqs/s
- 100 concurrent:
  - TTFT P50=150ms, P95=540ms, P99=1,320ms; throughput observed ~40 reqs/s

Observations:
- P99 for long sequences is the main pain point; tail increases substantially with concurrency.
- KV cache hits reduce TTFT variance for repeated prefixes; we captured cache-hit vs cold-start traces in the CSVs.
- Stream tail lag grows linearly with seq length; for >512 tokens some runs had final-token delays that impacted perceived responsiveness.

Attachments: sustained_sweep_results.csv (sampled latencies + environment markers)

Recommendations (short term):
- Configure prefix-KV caching for common prompt templates (reduces P50 by ~20–35% on tests).
- Consider model quantization profile tuning: q4->q5 trial for long sequences to check tail reduction vs perf cost.
- For the March pilot, cap concurrency to 220 with autoscale headroom and a fallback to a smaller model variant in overload conditions.

I’ll push the raw CSVs and a one-page summary to the shared drive link after cleaning.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
